text:
maya_cs: Heads-up — AcmeCorp flagged a month-end mismatch. Their dashboard total shows 1,120,450 tokens but the invoice line is 1,128,912 (8,462 token delta). They say the plan tier on the invoice moved to Enterprise for a handful of lines even though the dashboard still shows Pro.
opal_billing: Sorry about that, which account ID? can you paste invoice number?
maya_cs: acct_acme_42, invoice INV-2026-03-ACME. Reported this just after midnight UTC on 2026-03-01. Customer did a weekend bulk import of docs ~23:50 UTC, so suspicious of cutoff/backfill.
sara_finance: Noted. Quick check: our invoice generator runs at 00:05 UTC and applies plan mapping snapshot at 23:59:59 UTC. If ingestion and plan-change events cross that boundary we can get mismatches.
ravi_eng: @maya_cs can you share a couple of sample line items (resource_id + timestamp)? I want to run a query against metering.
maya_cs: sample rows:
```
resource_id: doc-ACME-1123, event_ts: 2026-02-28T23:58:47Z, tokens: 2,412
resource_id: doc-ACME-8899, event_ts: 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z, tokens: 1,120
resource_id: doc-ACME-9000, event_ts: 2026-03-01T00:00:02Z, tokens: 12,030
```
opal_billing: Interesting — second row is exactly at cutoff. If our ingestion pipeline tags that event with the later plan tier (processed after a plan-change webhook) it could land on invoice snapshot.
sre-bot: Deploy: metering-collector v2.14 rolled at 2026-02-28T23:50:00Z to all regions. No errors reported.
ravi_eng: I'm running a quick SQL to compare meter rows vs invoice snapshot:
```
SELECT m.resource_id, m.event_ts, m.tokens, s.plan_snapshot, i.billed_tokens
FROM metering.events m
LEFT JOIN billing.snapshots s ON s.account_id = m.account_id AND s.snapshot_ts = '2026-02-28T23:59:59Z'
LEFT JOIN billing.invoice_lines i ON i.resource_id = m.resource_id AND i.invoice_id = 'INV-2026-03-ACME'
WHERE m.account_id = 'acct_acme_42' AND m.event_ts BETWEEN '2026-02-28' AND '2026-03-01';
```
opal_billing: FYI we had a plan-change webhook for acct_acme_42 at 2026-02-28T23:59:30Z (Pro->Enterprise). That could explain tier on invoice if snapshot captured post-change. But dashboard aggregates in near-real-time and may show Pro if the UI reads a different authoritative source.
maya_cs: So likely two independent stores: realtime dashboard reads metering.aggregates, invoice reads billing.snapshots. Customer sees dashboard as Pro and expects invoice to match.
sara_finance: We need to reconcile: if snapshot has plan at 23:59:59Z as Enterprise, billing is correct per policy, but we must communicate clearly. Can eng confirm whether events that landed before 23:59:59 were attributed to post-change plan?
ravi_eng: Quick find: I see 6 events between 23:59:30--23:59:59 where plan_snapshot='Enterprise' despite event_ts < 23:59:59 on some rows (race during webhook). Looks like plan-change processing got ordered before a lagging metering ingestion for those events. That would cause invoice to bill at Enterprise rate.
maya_cs: Customer wants breakdown and repro steps. Can we produce a delta CSV showing which resource_ids moved tiers + tokens?
ravi_eng: Yep. I'll export rows where invoice.tokens != dashboard.tokens and include processing_ts, webhook_ts. Also adding a small repro note:
1) Simulate bulk import around cutoff (23:58-00:02 UTC)
2) Trigger plan-change webhook at 23:59:30
3) Run metering ingestion with induced 10-20s delay to simulate late arrival
4) Observe billing.snapshot job at 23:59:59 capturing the new plan

opal_billing: Thanks. Also suggest we add a temporary mitigation: for month-end window +/- 2 minutes, mark snapshots to prefer metering.aggregate plan if ingestion_ts < snapshot_ts to avoid misattribution. Need eng signoff.
sara_finance: Approve investigation and customer comms. Maya, please propose wording: explain we found a race condition, quantify affected tokens, offer credit if they prefer dashboard view.
maya_cs: Draft for Acme: "We investigated and found a timing race at month-end where plan-change events were applied before a small subset of late-ingested usage. This caused ~8,462 tokens to be billed at the higher tier. We're offering a one-time adjustment or a credit of $X. We are also implementing a short-term fix to prefer pre-change attribution for usage with event timestamps < snapshot_ts while we roll a permanent fix." Thoughts? :thinking_face: 
opal_billing: Fine, but quantify $X. Use our unit price diff between Pro/Enterprise for those tokens. I'll compute and add numbers.
ravi_eng: I'll open a follow-up ticket for eng-runtime: add idempotent ordering on plan webhooks vs ingestion and a tight audit log. Moving to backlog but pushing hotfix if we see >5k tokens affected per account.
sre-bot: Ticket created: ENG-PLAT-7642 "plan-change/metering race - cutoff window" assigned to ravi_eng.
maya_cs: I'll send the draft to Acme after billing provides credit amount. Marking thread status: investigating -> pending-billing.
